parsed.explanation: The dossier is thin on trans-specific matters. It documents no trans-specific offence, no gender-marker or facility rule, no targeting by police or border officers, and no trans-specific violence. Silence on those axes is not evidence of safety, so I extrapolate from structural signals. The repealed sexuality sections were never recorded as enforced in living memory, and the repeal bill cited growing LGBT acceptance, so the criminal exposure is dated and dead-letter. Parliamentary and select-committee processes appear to function. Against this, the 2000 marriage law and the stalled reform (members reversed a deletion and deferred the bill) show a conservative undercurrent, and the penalty figures conflict. Visitor-facing exposure such as document checks and facility rules is unresolved. Overall this reads as reduced risk at the lower end of that band.
